\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p(\zeta^k)
=
\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\left(\zeta^{kn}+a_{n-1}\zeta^{k(n-1)}+\cdots+a_1\zeta^k+1\right).
\]

Since \(\zeta^{kn}=1\) and \(\zeta^k\neq 1\) for \(1\le k\le n-1\),

\[
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\zeta^{km}=0 \qquad (1\le m\le n-1).
\]

Thus all intermediate terms vanish in the average, leaving

\[
\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p(\zeta^k)
=
\frac1n(n+n)=2.
\]

Therefore, by the triangle inequality,

\[
2
=
\left|\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p(\zeta^k)\right|
\le
\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}|p(\zeta^k)|
\le
\max_{|z|=1}|p(z)|.
\]

So every \(p\in S_n\) satisfies

\[
\max_{|z|=1}|p(z)|\ge 2.
\]

On the other hand, the polynomial

\[
p_0(z)=z^n+1
\]

belongs to \(S_n\), and for \(|z|=1\),

\[
|p_0(z)|=|z^n+1|\le 2,
\]

with equality at \(z=1\). Hence

\[
\max_{|z|=1}|p_0(z)|=2.
\]

Combining the lower and upper bounds gives

\[
M_n=2.
\]

\[
\boxed{2}
\]

27B·v4.method: Average p over n-th roots of unity to isolate leading and constant coefficients (sum=2), giving lower bound 2; polynomial zⁿ+1 achieves upper bound 2.
